title: Why Contacts Matter
learningGoal: Understand why the Contacts page is one of the most important areas in LeadProspectrr.

items.title: Central Hub
items.description: The Contacts page is where all your leads, customers, and prospects live — it's the foundation of your CRM.

items.title: Relationship Tracking
items.description: Every interaction, note, and detail about a person is stored here, giving you a complete picture of your relationships.

items.title: Revenue Potential
items.description: Well-organized contacts lead to better follow-up, which directly impacts your sales and customer retention.

items.title: Navigate with Confidence
items.description: Learn to move through the Contacts page quickly and find exactly what you need.

items.title: Organize Effectively
items.description: Use tags, filters, and Smart Lists to keep your contacts organized and actionable.

items.title: Take Action
items.description: Turn contact data into follow-up tasks and meaningful conversations.

keyPoint: Your contacts are more than just names and emails — they're real people with real potential. Treating your Contacts page as a priority will transform how you do business.

actionSteps.title: Log into LeadProspectrr
actionSteps.description: Navigate to your Contacts page and take a moment to look at what you currently have there.

actionSteps.title: Count Your Contacts
actionSteps.description: Note how many contacts you currently have and think about where they came from.

actionSteps.title: Identify One Goal
actionSteps.description: Write down one thing you want to improve about how you manage contacts this week.

quizzes.question: Why is the Contacts page considered the heart of LeadProspectrr?

options.option_text: It's the only page you can access
It stores all your leads, customers, and prospect information in one place
It has the best design
It's required by law

quizzes.explanation: The Contacts page is central because it houses all your relationship data — leads, customers, and prospects — making it the foundation for all your CRM activities.

title: Review the Contacts Page
learningGoal: Learn what to look for on the Contacts page and understand the information displayed.

items.title: Contact List
items.description: The main area shows your contacts with key details like name, email, phone, and tags visible at a glance.

items.title: Search Bar
items.description: Quickly find contacts by name, email, phone number, or company using the search functionality.

items.title: View Controls
items.description: Customize which columns display, adjust the number of rows shown, and sort by different fields.

items.title: Tags
items.description: Visual indicators showing how contacts are categorized (e.g., 'Lead', 'Customer', 'Hot Prospect').

items.title: Last Activity
items.description: See when you last interacted with each contact to prioritize follow-ups.

items.title: Status Indicators
items.description: Quick visual cues showing lead source, engagement level, or pipeline stage.

keyPoint: The Contacts page is designed to give you a bird's-eye view of your entire database while making it easy to drill down into specific details when needed.

actionSteps.title: Explore the Layout
actionSteps.description: Spend 2 minutes clicking through different areas of the Contacts page to see what's available.

actionSteps.title: Try the Search
actionSteps.description: Use the search bar to find a specific contact by name or email.

actionSteps.title: Customize Your View
actionSteps.description: Click on the column settings and adjust which fields are visible to match your workflow.

quizzes.question: What information is typically visible on the main Contacts page list view?

options.option_text: Only the contact's name
Name, email, phone, tags, and last activity
Full conversation history
Bank account details

quizzes.explanation: The Contacts page list view displays key information at a glance including name, email, phone, tags, and last activity — enough to identify and prioritize contacts without opening each record.

title: Open a Contact Record
learningGoal: Learn how to open and review an individual contact record to understand the full story of a person.

items.title: Click to Open
items.description: Click on any contact's name in the list to open their full record and see complete details.

items.title: Quick Access
items.description: Use the search to find a contact, then click their name to jump directly to their record.

items.title: From Other Pages
items.description: Contact names are linked throughout the system — click them from tasks, appointments, or pipeline views.

items.title: Contact Details
items.description: Full name, email, phone numbers, address, company, job title, and custom fields.

items.title: Activity Timeline
items.description: A chronological view of all interactions, notes, emails, calls, and appointments.

items.title: Tags and Segments
items.description: See which tags are applied and what Smart Lists this contact belongs to.

items.title: Tasks and Opportunities
items.description: View open tasks, upcoming appointments, and pipeline opportunities for this contact.

keyPoint: A contact record tells the complete story of your relationship with a person — every interaction, note, and detail in one place.

actionSteps.title: Open Three Records
actionSteps.description: Click on three different contacts to open their full records and compare what you see.

actionSteps.title: Review the Timeline
actionSteps.description: Scroll through the Activity Timeline to see the history of interactions with one contact.

actionSteps.title: Check for Completeness
actionSteps.description: Note which contacts have complete information and which are missing key details.

quizzes.question: What can you find inside a contact record?

options.option_text: Only the contact's email address
Complete details, activity timeline, tags, tasks, and opportunities
Just their profile picture
System settings

quizzes.explanation: A contact record contains the complete picture: contact details, activity timeline, tags, tasks, and opportunities — everything you need to understand and engage with that person.

title: Understand Key Contact Details
learningGoal: Understand the most important fields inside a contact record and how they help with organization and follow-up.

items.title: Basic Information
items.description: First name, last name, email, and phone are the foundation — ensure these are accurate for every contact.

items.title: Address Details
items.description: Physical address helps with local targeting, shipping, and understanding your geographic reach.

items.title: Company & Title
items.description: Knowing where someone works and their role helps tailor your messaging and identify decision-makers.

items.title: Tags
items.description: Labels like 'Hot Lead', 'Customer', or 'Newsletter' help you segment and take targeted action.

items.title: Lead Source
items.description: Knowing where a contact came from (website, referral, social media) helps you understand what works.

items.title: Custom Date Fields
items.description: Birthdays, anniversaries, or follow-up dates trigger timely outreach and build relationships.

items.title: Notes
items.description: Free-form notes capture context, preferences, and details that don't fit in structured fields.

keyPoint: The quality of your contact data directly impacts your ability to follow up effectively. Focus on keeping essential fields accurate and complete.

actionSteps.title: Audit Five Contacts
actionSteps.description: Open five contact records and check if essential fields (name, email, phone) are complete.

actionSteps.title: Review Tags
actionSteps.description: Check if your contacts have appropriate tags applied — are they categorized correctly?

actionSteps.title: Add Missing Information
actionSteps.description: Update at least three contacts with any missing key details you have available.

quizzes.question: Why are tags important in contact records?

options.option_text: They make the page look colorful
They help segment contacts and enable targeted action
They are required by the system
They automatically send emails

quizzes.explanation: Tags are powerful organizational tools that let you categorize contacts (like 'Hot Lead' or 'Customer') so you can filter, search, and take targeted actions on specific groups.

title: Tags, Filters, and Smart Lists
learningGoal: Understand the difference between tags, filters, and Smart Lists and how they work together.

items.title: What Are Tags?
items.description: Tags are labels you apply to individual contacts to categorize them (e.g., 'Lead', 'Customer', 'VIP').

items.title: Manual Application
items.description: Tags are typically applied manually or through automation — they stick with the contact.

items.title: Multiple Tags
items.description: A contact can have multiple tags, allowing for flexible categorization.

items.title: What Are Filters?
items.description: Filters are temporary criteria you apply to see a subset of contacts right now.

items.title: Not Saved
items.description: Unless you save them, filters disappear when you navigate away or clear them.

items.title: Powerful Criteria
items.description: Filter by tags, dates, custom fields, lead source, and more.

items.title: What Are Smart Lists?
items.description: Smart Lists are saved filters that update automatically as contacts meet or don't meet criteria.

items.title: Reusable
items.description: Create once, use forever — Smart Lists are always available in your sidebar.

items.title: Dynamic Updates
items.description: Contacts automatically appear or disappear from Smart Lists as their data changes.

keyPoint: Tags label your contacts, filters find them, and Smart Lists remember your searches. Together, they create a powerful system for organizing and engaging with your database.

actionSteps.title: Review Your Tags
actionSteps.description: Look at what tags currently exist in your account and how they're being used.

actionSteps.title: Try a Filter
actionSteps.description: Click the filter button and experiment with filtering by a tag or date range.

actionSteps.title: Check Existing Smart Lists
actionSteps.description: Look at any Smart Lists already in your account to understand how they're set up.

nextLessonTitle: Before You Build a Smart List

quizzes.question: What is the key difference between a filter and a Smart List?

options.option_text: There is no difference
Filters are temporary, Smart Lists are saved and update automatically
Filters are for experts only
Smart Lists cost extra

quizzes.explanation: Filters are temporary views that disappear when you navigate away, while Smart Lists are saved filters that persist and automatically update as contacts meet or don't meet the criteria.

title: Before You Build a Smart List
learningGoal: Plan the Smart List before creating it to ensure it stays useful.

items.title: Why This List?
items.description: Ask yourself: What will I do with the contacts in this list? Will I email them? Call them? Track them?

items.title: Name It Clearly
items.description: Give your Smart List a descriptive name that explains who it contains (e.g., 'Hot Leads - No Contact in 7 Days').

items.title: Test the Value
items.description: If you can't think of a specific action you'll take with this list, reconsider whether you need it.

items.title: Which Tags?
items.description: Will you filter by specific tags? Make sure those tags are consistently applied.

items.title: Date Ranges?
items.description: Do you need contacts from a specific time period or with certain date field values?

items.title: Custom Fields?
items.description: Will you filter by lead source, status, or other custom field values?

items.title: Multiple Conditions?
items.description: Do you need AND conditions (must meet all) or OR conditions (can meet any)?

keyPoint: A Smart List without a clear purpose becomes clutter. Always know WHY you're building it and WHAT you'll do with it before you start.

actionSteps.title: Choose a Purpose
actionSteps.description: Decide on one specific follow-up action you want to take (e.g., 'Call hot leads who haven't been contacted in a week').

actionSteps.title: Write Down Criteria
actionSteps.description: List the specific conditions a contact must meet to be on this list.

actionSteps.title: Name Your List
actionSteps.description: Create a clear, descriptive name that you'll recognize in 6 months.

quizzes.question: Why is it important to plan your Smart List before building it?

options.option_text: It's required by the system
To ensure it has a clear purpose and will actually be useful
Planning makes it load faster
You can't edit it after creation

quizzes.explanation: Planning ensures your Smart List has a clear purpose and specific action associated with it. Without this, Smart Lists become unused clutter that doesn't drive your business forward.

title: Build Your Filters
learningGoal: Learn how to use filters to find a specific group of contacts.

items.title: Open Filters
items.description: Click the 'Filter' button on the Contacts page to open the filter panel.

items.title: Add Conditions
items.description: Click 'Add Filter' to start building your criteria. You can add multiple conditions.

items.title: Apply Filters
items.description: Click 'Apply' to see the filtered results update in real-time.

items.title: Tag Filters
items.description: Filter by one or more tags. Use 'contains any' for OR logic or 'contains all' for AND logic.

items.title: Date Filters
items.description: Filter by created date, last activity, or custom date fields with ranges like 'last 7 days' or 'before date'.

items.title: Field Filters
items.description: Filter by any contact field: email contains, phone is empty, company equals, etc.

items.title: Source Filters
items.description: Filter by lead source, pipeline stage, or campaign membership.

items.title: Review the Count
items.description: Check how many contacts match your criteria — too many or too few may mean adjusting filters.

items.title: Adjust as Needed
items.description: Add, remove, or modify filter conditions until you get exactly the group you want.

items.title: Verify Sample Contacts
items.description: Spot-check a few contacts in the results to confirm they should be included.

keyPoint: Building good filters is about balancing specificity with usefulness — narrow enough to be actionable, broad enough to be valuable.

actionSteps.title: Open the Filter Panel
actionSteps.description: Navigate to Contacts and click the Filter button to see available options.

actionSteps.title: Build One Filter
actionSteps.description: Create a filter using the criteria you planned in the previous lesson.

actionSteps.title: Refine Until Right
actionSteps.description: Adjust your filters until the contact count feels right for your intended action.

quizzes.question: What should you do if your filter returns too many or too few contacts?

options.option_text: Delete the contacts
Adjust the filter conditions until you get the right group size
Contact support
Start over with a new account

quizzes.explanation: Filter refinement is part of the process. Adjust your conditions — make them more specific to reduce results or broader to increase them — until you have an actionable group size.

title: Save the Smart List
learningGoal: Save a filtered view so it can be used again later.

items.title: Click Save
items.description: Once your filter shows the right contacts, click 'Save as Smart List' to preserve it.

items.title: Name It
items.description: Use the descriptive name you planned earlier — clear names prevent confusion later.

items.title: Confirm Save
items.description: Click Save and verify the Smart List appears in your sidebar.

items.title: Naming Conventions
items.description: Consider a naming pattern like 'Action - Description' (e.g., 'Call - Hot Leads 7 Days').

items.title: Group by Purpose
items.description: Use consistent prefixes to group related Smart Lists together in the sidebar.

items.title: Avoid Duplicates
items.description: Check existing Smart Lists before creating new ones to prevent clutter.

items.title: Click to View
items.description: Click your new Smart List in the sidebar to confirm it loads the expected contacts.

items.title: Check Auto-Update
items.description: Understand that this list will automatically update as contacts meet or don't meet criteria.

items.title: Verify Access
items.description: Make sure the Smart List is easily accessible for regular use.

keyPoint: Saving a Smart List transforms a one-time filter into a permanent tool that keeps working for you automatically.

actionSteps.title: Save Your Filter
actionSteps.description: Click 'Save as Smart List' and give it a clear, descriptive name.

actionSteps.title: Verify in Sidebar
actionSteps.description: Check that your new Smart List appears in the sidebar and click it to test.

actionSteps.title: Document the Purpose
actionSteps.description: Write down what action you'll take with this Smart List so you remember later.

quizzes.question: What happens when you save a filter as a Smart List?

options.option_text: The contacts are permanently locked in the list
It becomes a reusable, automatically updating saved view
It sends an email to all contacts
It deletes the filter

quizzes.explanation: Saving a filter as a Smart List creates a permanent, reusable view that automatically updates as contacts meet or no longer meet the criteria — it's a living list, not a static snapshot.

title: Use Your Smart List
learningGoal: Understand how Smart Lists can support follow-up and contact management.

items.title: Start Your Day
items.description: Check your key Smart Lists each morning to see who needs attention today.

items.title: Batch Your Actions
items.description: Use Smart Lists to group similar tasks — make all your calls, then send all your emails.

items.title: Track Progress
items.description: Watch the list shrink as you complete follow-ups, giving you a sense of accomplishment.

items.title: Call Lists
items.description: Create Smart Lists for contacts due for a call based on last contact date.

items.title: Email Campaigns
items.description: Build lists of contacts who should receive specific email sequences.

items.title: Follow-up Reminders
items.description: Identify contacts who haven't been contacted in a set number of days.

items.title: Segmented Outreach
items.description: Target specific groups like 'New Leads This Week' or 'Customers for Upsell'.

keyPoint: Smart Lists turn your contact database into an action-oriented system — they tell you WHO to contact and WHEN, making follow-up systematic instead of sporadic.

actionSteps.title: Open Your Smart List
actionSteps.description: Click on the Smart List you created and review the contacts it contains.

actionSteps.title: Plan Your Actions
actionSteps.description: Decide what you'll do with each contact on the list (call, email, tag, etc.).

actionSteps.title: Take Action on Three
actionSteps.description: Contact at least three people from your Smart List using the appropriate method.

quizzes.question: How can Smart Lists support your daily workflow?

options.option_text: They automatically send emails for you
They help you identify who needs attention and batch your actions
They replace the Contacts page entirely
They delete old contacts automatically

quizzes.explanation: Smart Lists help you identify which contacts need attention and enable you to batch similar actions together — like making all your calls at once — making your workflow more efficient and systematic.

title: Edit and Reuse Smart Lists
learningGoal: Learn how to reuse and update Smart Lists over time.

items.title: Edit Criteria
items.description: Open a Smart List and click Edit to change the filter conditions — add, remove, or modify criteria.

items.title: Rename When Needed
items.description: If the purpose of a Smart List changes, update its name to reflect the new use.

items.title: Review Regularly
items.description: Periodically check your Smart Lists to ensure they're still relevant and useful.

items.title: Duplicate for Variations
items.description: Save time by duplicating an existing Smart List and modifying it for a similar purpose.

items.title: Template Approach
items.description: Create template Smart Lists with common criteria patterns you use frequently.

items.title: Share with Team
items.description: Ensure team members know about useful Smart Lists and how to use them.

items.title: Audit Quarterly
items.description: Review all Smart Lists every few months — delete unused ones, update outdated criteria.

items.title: Document Purpose
items.description: Keep notes on what each Smart List is for, especially if you have many.

items.title: Iterate and Improve
items.description: As your business evolves, update Smart Lists to match new processes and priorities.

keyPoint: Smart Lists are living tools that should evolve with your business. Regular maintenance ensures they stay useful and don't become digital clutter.

actionSteps.title: Review Your Smart Lists
actionSteps.description: Look at all Smart Lists in your account and identify any that need updating or deleting.

actionSteps.title: Edit One List
actionSteps.description: Choose one Smart List and modify its criteria to better match your current needs.

actionSteps.title: Create a Variation
actionSteps.description: Duplicate an existing Smart List and adjust it for a slightly different purpose.

quizzes.question: Why is it important to regularly review and update your Smart Lists?

options.option_text: The system requires it every week
To ensure they stay relevant and useful as your business evolves
They stop working after 30 days
To free up storage space

quizzes.explanation: Regular review ensures your Smart Lists remain relevant as your business processes, priorities, and contact data evolve. Outdated Smart Lists become clutter and may miss important contacts or include irrelevant ones.
